headline: Braves walk off Phillies 6-5 in 11 innings
recap: The Phillies lost an 11-inning back-and-forth game to the Braves 6-5 at Truist Park on Friday night. Matt Olson's leadoff-inning solo homer, his 38th of the season, put Atlanta up 1-0, but Philadelphia answered in the top of the second when Derek Hill's bases-clearing double drove in Edmundo Sosa, Bryan De La Cruz and J.T. Realmuto for a 3-1 lead. Austin Riley's solo homer in the seventh, his 17th, cut the margin to 3-2, and Sean Murphy tied it 3-3 in the ninth on a single to center that scored DaShawn Keirsey Jr. after center fielder Derek Hill misplayed the ball for an error, which also let Murphy reach second. The lead changed hands twice more in extra innings: Justin Crawford's RBI single scored Bryson Stott in the top of the tenth before Mauricio Dubon's sacrifice fly brought home Brewer Hicklen to tie it again, and Luis Arraez's RBI single put the Phillies back ahead 5-4 in the top of the eleventh only for Ha-Seong Kim to tie it right back with an RBI single in the bottom half. Drake Baldwin then doubled home Kim for the winning run and the 6-5 final. Aaron Nola started and allowed two earned runs over 6.1 innings with three strikeouts; Brooks Raley (loss) was the pitcher of record when the Braves finished it off.
The loss dropped Philadelphia to 82-66, second in the NL East, five games behind the division-leading Braves. The Phillies have now lost two straight.

Philadelphia continues the series at Atlanta tonight, with first pitch at Truist Park scheduled for 7:15 PM ET. The Phillies had not yet announced a starter as of this writing; Tyler Mahle is set to go for the Braves. No betting line was available for the game.
